Q: Meta Threads API exchange access tokens in error A:

I had a similar issue when i had published my app before the review had approved everything.
Just try to unpublish / re-publish your app especially if all your review is approved.

Note: this may trigger a renewal access but i think it's after some time because it didn't trigger it for me and i could unpublish - re-publish immediately and everything was working fine.

Q: How can I take a screenshot of a full page with Playwright (visual comparison)? A:

The existing answer covers fullPage: true for Playwright's built-in visual comparison.

If you're capturing screenshots for documentation rather than visual regresion testing, you might want element-level screenshots rather than full pages:

npx heroshot https://playwright.dev --selector ".hero" -o hero-section.png

Playwright's toHaveScreenshot() is designed for pixel-diff testing (it fails on differences). For documentation screenshots that you want to update when the UI changes, a capture tool like heroshot is a better fit. They produce the images rather than comparing them.

Q: Selenium Webdriver (node.js) take screenshot and save test results A:

The accepted answer covers Selenium's takeScreenshot() well for test failures.

If your goal is specifically capturing screenshots of your app (for docs, changelogs, or visual records) rather than test failure screenshots, consider config-driven tools that handle this at scle:

# One-liner: screenshot a URL
npx heroshot https://myapp.com -o screenshot.png

# From config file: capture 20+ pages at once
npx heroshot

Heroshot separates "screenshot capture" from "test execution". You don't need a test framework just to take screenshots.

Q: Next.js 16 App Router PWA + Supabase SSR: infinite loading on mobile/PWA (manual service worker likely caching RSC/Flight) A:

It's very likely your service worker is interfering with App Router's RSC/Flight requests or auth redirects.

If you use Next.js 16 (App Router), you should not cache or intercept anything dynamic.

  • Navigation requests

  • RSC/Flight requests (text/x-component, RSC, Next-Router-State-Tree headers)

  • Auth-protected routes

  • API calls

Even a "NetworkFirst" or navigation fetch() inside the SW can break redirect handing (302 from middleware) and cause Suspense to hang -> infinite loading / blank screen, which shows up more often in mobile/PWA.
For App Router + Supabase SSR, please keep the service worker minimal.

  • Cache only /_next/static/* (CacheFirst)

  • Optionally cache images/icons

  • Let everything else go straight to the network (don't intercept)

In authenticated SSR apps, treating the Service work as an asset cache only is the safest approach.

Q: Screenshot for each DOM node A:

The accepted answer shows elementHandle.screenshot() which is the right Puppeteer API.

If you want to screenshot specific elements across a site (not literaly every DOM node), tools like heroshot have a visual picker that lets you click elements in a browser and automatically captures their selectors:

npx heroshot
# Opens browser, navigate to your site, click elements
# Generates config with selectors + screenshots

This avoids the problem of programmatically finding meaningful selectors. You pick them visually instead.

Q: How do I generate documentation screenshots for a Qt application? A:

For web-based documentation screenshots, config-driven tools like heroshot or shot-scraper solve this - define screenshots in config, regenerate with make docs.

For desktop Qt applications specifically, your options are:

  1. QTest + QWidget::grab() — Qt's test framework can launch your app, navigate to the right state, and capture widgets:
QPixmap pixmap = widget->grab();
pixmap.save("docs/screenshots/main-window.png");

  1. Squish or other GUI test tools - Commercial tools like Froglogic Squish support screenshot capture as part of GUI test scripts.

  2. Platform screenshot tools in scripts - Use xdotool (Linux) or screencapture (macOS) in your Makefile after launching the app in a known state.

The key principle you mentioned — keeping screenshots as generated artifacts rather than committed PNGs - is the right approach. Add the screenshot generation to your make documentation target so they're always current.
